title: AI and The End of Scarcity
lines: AI and The End of Scarcity asks when greater efficiency could become shared abundance.
Its vision is conditional on infrastructure, institutions, and access.
That makes the distribution of gains as important as technological capability.

title: A forecast is not a meal
lines: Imagine forecasting food demand more accurately and wasting fewer supplies.
That improves a process, but does not decide who receives the food.
The book uses distribution to expose this gap between efficiency and fairness.

title: The physical system remains
lines: Energy forecasts still need grids and storage; reuse still needs collection and repair.
The chapters connect manufacturing, logistics, energy, and circular production.
They invite readers to test particular improvements rather than assume one universal breakthrough.

title: Judge the conditions
lines: Read it as a set of possibilities to assess, rather than a prediction of inevitability.
Start with scarcity, then compare the distribution and ethics chapters.
Ask which practical and institutional conditions each proposed gain would require.
